note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Adult with known childhood asthma presenting with 2–3 days of cough, subjective fever, and increased wheeze/shortness of breath consistent with an acute asthma flare.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Acute wheeze and shortness of breath for 2–3 days.
  - Frequent coughing and reported fever.
  - Reduced exercise tolerance — unable to walk to work; sometimes cannot complete sentences when breathless.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms began 2–3 days prior to consultation and are recent; patient reports intermittent worsening with exertion but felt relatively well at the time of the call.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Exacerbated by walking/exertion.
  - No specific relieving factors documented; doctor advised increasing inhaler use and obtaining spacer.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Cough without sputum production.
  - No hemoptysis reported.
  - No chest pain.
  - No night-time wakening due to symptoms.
- Systems review / pertinent negatives:
  - Denies chest pain.
  - Denies sputum production or blood when coughing.
  - Denies nocturnal symptoms.
  - No other systems symptoms documented.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma:
  - Childhood history of asthma described as “quite bad.”
  - Required hospital visits sometimes in the past for asthma; never required ICU.
  - Patient reports prior use of inhalers; timeframe inconsistent (see conflicts).
- Allergic rhinitis (hay fever).
- Eczema.
- Medications explicitly mentioned:
  - Salbutamol — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies:
  - No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Smoking: Denies tobacco smoking.
- Alcohol: Drinks a glass of wine approximately every 2–3 days.
- Living situation: Lives with partner.
- Occupation: Engineer.
- Work impact: Unable to walk to work recently; working from home or taking sick leave.

Family History:
- No family history information provided / none mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals:
  - Patient-reported temperature: 37°C (patient stated they had a fever; measured/reported as 37°C).
- Examination findings:
  - No formal physical exam findings documented in the transcript.

Investigations:
- No objective investigations, imaging, or test results documented.
- Plan to prescribe peak flow meter for home monitoring (not yet performed).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute asthma exacerbation / wheeze
  - Assessment:
    - Probable asthma flare given history of asthma, increased wheeze, exertional dyspnea, cough; possible triggers include viral infection or seasonal allergen exposure.
  - Plan:
    - Increase use of bronchodilator inhaler (salbutamol) more regularly — suggested regimen: 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially (dose/route/frequency as discussed verbally; prescription specifics not documented).
    - Prescribe a spacer to improve inhaler delivery; pharmacist to demonstrate correct use.
    - Prescribe a peak flow meter for home monitoring; patient instructed to record peak flow first thing in the morning and in the evening over the next week.
    - Arrange review (telephone) in approximately one week to review peak flow values and clinical progress; consider initiation of additional controller inhaler if required.
    - Instruct patient to contact services urgently if wheeze worsens or if high temperature develops.
- Issue 2: Subjective fever / possible viral illness
  - Assessment:
    - Patient reports fever but measured temperature recorded as 37°C during the call.
  - Plan:
    - Monitor temperature at home.
    - Advise to call back immediately if temperature rises significantly or respiratory status deteriorates.
- Issue 3: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever) contributing to symptoms
  - Assessment:
    - Ongoing history of hay fever.
  - Plan:
    - Start a regular antihistamine available from pharmacy; doctor offered to note recommended medication on record (specific antihistamine name/dose not documented).
- General plan items:
  - Pharmacist to demonstrate spacer and peak flow meter use.
  - Patient to document peak flow readings morning and evening for the next week and bring/read out figures during planned review.
  - Consider stepping up asthma therapy after review if symptoms/peak flow warrant.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note, or fill document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Objective respiratory examination (auscultation), oxygen saturation, heart rate, respiratory rate, and blood pressure are not documented.
  - Exact current inhaler possession and confirmation of reliever vs controller inhaler in use unclear.
  - Doses, routes, and frequency for salbutamol and the recommended antihistamine are not documented.
  - No baseline or subsequent peak flow values recorded at the time of consult.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Patient initially implied asthma stopped ~3–4 years ago, but later stated they “normally” take salbutamol — conflict noted regarding current inhaler use history.
  - Patient reported having a fever yet reported a measured temperature of 37°C (low/normal) — conflict noted between subjective fever and measured temperature.
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall intelligible with some brief hesitations and minor repetitions; adequate for clinical information extraction.
